create.name: Brother Phap Linh
create.bio:
Brother Phap Linh, often called Brother Spirit, is a Zen monk in the Plum Village community of Thich Nhat Hanh in the south-west of France. Before taking robes he read mathematics at Cambridge and earned his living as a composer in London. He entered monastic training at Plum Village in early 2008, and since then he has written a large share of the chants the community sings today. He also helped to start Wake Up, the Plum Village network for practitioners aged roughly eighteen to thirty-five.

His talks tend to join Buddhist practice with present-day questions: how to meet the climate crisis without burning out, what neuroscience can and cannot tell us about meditation, and how to choose a meaningful direction in life when the world feels unsteady. He teaches applied mindfulness to groups of activists, artists, scientists and people in business, and leads sessions and talks during the retreats held at Plum Village, many of which are filmed and shared freely. In the free Plum Village app he guides eating meditations, compassionate listening and long deep relaxations, some set to cello music he composed and plays himself. He writes now and then for The Mindfulness Bell.

free_resources.title: 42-Minute Deep Relaxation (with Cello)
free_resources.description: A long guided rest lying down, in which he invites the listener to feel the ground supporting the body. It closes with a cello piece he wrote and performs. Free to stream in the web edition of the Plum Village app.

free_resources.title: 46-Minute Neuroscience Deep Relaxation
free_resources.description: A guided body scan shaped by what is known about the nervous system, spending longer on the areas of the body richest in nerve endings to help attention settle. Free to stream in the Plum Village app.

free_resources.title: Tangerine Meditation
free_resources.description: A four-minute eating practice from the Plum Village tradition. Holding a piece of fruit, the listener reflects on everything that went into bringing it to their hands.

free_resources.title: Listening, Speaking and Looking with Compassion
free_resources.description: A short guided practice on bringing deep listening, kind speech and a gentle way of seeing into relationships with others.
